name: VISIBLE SPECTROPHOTOMETER
desc: Benchtop Digital Visible Spectrophotometer engineered for routine photometric analysis, quantitative chemical assays, and quality control processing. Features a compact, highly portable single beam optical layout optimized for the visible spectrum range with a built-in USB data output port.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Visible Spectrophotometer operates on the principle of single-beam optical absorption spectroscopy within the visible spectrum (typically 320–1100 nm). A tungsten-halogen lamp emits polychromatic light, which is collimated and passed through a monochromator (diffraction grating) to isolate a narrow band of wavelengths. The monochromatic beam is then split: one path passes through the reference blank (solvent or reagent blank), and the other through the sample cuvette. A silicon photodiode detector measures the intensity of transmitted light for both paths. The instrument computes Transmittance (%T = I/I₀ × 100) and Absorbance (A = -log₁₀ T) based on the Beer-Lambert law (A = ε·c·l), where ε is molar absorptivity, c is concentration, and l is path length. Concentration mode uses a pre-calibrated standard curve or factor. This benchtop unit is engineered for routine photometric analysis, quantitative chemical assays, and quality control processing in clinical laboratories (e.g., serum bilirubin, hemoglobin, glucose via enzymatic colorimetric kits), academic research (B.Sc/M.Sc/PhD studies of transition metal complexes, dye degradation kinetics, enzyme activity assays like alkaline phosphatase), and industrial QC (testing of food colorants, textile dyes, pharmaceutical actives like paracetamol, and water quality parameters such as nitrate and phosphate). It supports compliance with ISO 13485 for medical device QC, ASTM E169-04 for UV-Vis quantitative analysis, and USP <857> for spectrophotometer performance verification. The single-beam design ensures high stability and low stray light, while the USB port enables direct data logging to LIMS or Excel for traceability.
sop: Ensure the instrument is placed on a stable, vibration-free bench away from direct sunlight and corrosive fumes. Connect the power cord to a 220-230 V AC, 50 Hz grounded outlet and switch ON the main power.
Allow the spectrophotometer to warm up for at least 15–20 minutes to stabilize the lamp and electronics. The digital display will show the last used wavelength and mode.
Press the 'MODE' button to select the desired measurement mode: Transmittance (%T), Absorbance (A), or Concentration (C). The selected mode will be indicated on the display.
Press the 'SET' button once. The wavelength display will start blinking, indicating that the target wavelength can be adjusted.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., set wavelength to 540 nm for hemoglobin assay or 510 nm for glucose). Press 'SET' again to lock the value.

Open the sample compartment lid and insert a cuvette filled with the blank solution (distilled water or reagent blank) into the sample holder. Ensure the cuvette's transparent sides are aligned with the light path and close the lid.
Press the 'ZERO' or 'BLANK' button to calibrate the instrument to 100%T or 0.000 A at the set wavelength. Wait until the display stabilizes.

Remove the blank cuvette, rinse a clean cuvette with a small portion of the sample solution, then fill it to about 2/3 capacity. Wipe the outer surfaces with lint-free tissue to remove fingerprints or droplets.

Insert the sample cuvette into the holder in the same orientation as the blank, close the lid, and read the displayed value for %T, Absorbance, or Concentration. Record the reading manually or via USB to a connected computer.

For multiple samples, repeat steps 7–9, re-zeroing with the blank every 10–15 samples or whenever the wavelength is changed. Always use matched cuvettes or the same cuvette for blank and sample to minimize path length errors.

After completing measurements, remove the last cuvette, switch OFF the instrument using the main power switch, and unplug if not in use for extended periods. Clean any spills immediately with a dry cloth.

SAFETY WARNING: Never operate the spectrophotometer with the sample compartment lid open during measurement, as stray UV/visible light can damage eyes and cause erroneous readings. Always handle strong acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄), organic solvents (e.g., acetone, ethanol), and biohazardous samples inside a fume hood or biosafety cabinet, and wear appropriate PPE (gloves, lab coat, safety goggles). Do not use glass cuvettes with hydrofluoric acid or highly alkaline solutions; use quartz or polymer cuvettes as specified. In case of chemical spill inside the sample compartment, power off immediately and clean with a mild detergent, then dry thoroughly before reuse.
